# Example 6: $(\Box A \vee \Box B) \rightarrow \Box(A \vee B)$ in K

## Example 6: $(\Box A \vee \Box B) \rightarrow \Box(A \vee B)$ in K

---

\begin{oltableau}
[\sFmla{\False}{1, (\Box A \lor \Box B) \rightarrow \Box(A \lor B)}, checked, just = \TAss
    [\sFmla{\True}{1, \Box A \lor \Box B}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\rightarrow}[1]}
        [\sFmla{\False}{1, \Box(A \lor B)}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\rightarrow}[1]}
        ]
    ]
]
\end{oltableau}

::: {.content-visible when-format="revealjs"}
![$(\Box A \lor \Box B) \rightarrow \Box(A \lor B)$](../images/tableaux-11/tableau-11-21.tex.svg){width=600px}
:::

False conditional: true antecedent and false consequent.

---

\begin{oltableau}
[\sFmla{\False}{1, (\Box A \lor \Box B) \rightarrow \Box(A \lor B)}, checked, just = \TAss
    [\sFmla{\True}{1, \Box A \lor \Box B}, checked, just = {\TRule{\False}{\rightarrow}[1]}
        [\sFmla{\False}{1, \Box(A \lor B)}, checked, just = {\TRule{\False}{\rightarrow}[1]}
            [\sFmla{\True}{1, \Box A}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\lor}[2]}
            ]
            [\sFmla{\True}{1, \Box B}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\lor}[2]}
            ]
        ]
    ]
]
\end{oltableau}

::: {.content-visible when-format="revealjs"}
![$(\Box A \lor \Box B) \rightarrow \Box(A \lor B)$](../images/tableaux-11/tableau-11-22.tex.svg){width=600px}
:::

The true disjunction branches: left branch has $\Box A$, right branch has $\Box B$. Work on the left branch first.

---

\begin{oltableau}
[\sFmla{\False}{1, (\Box A \lor \Box B) \rightarrow \Box(A \lor B)}, checked, just = \TAss
    [\sFmla{\True}{1, \Box A \lor \Box B}, checked, just = {\TRule{\False}{\rightarrow}[1]}
        [\sFmla{\False}{1, \Box(A \lor B)}, checked, just = {\TRule{\False}{\rightarrow}[1]}
            [\sFmla{\True}{1, \Box A}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\lor}[2]}
                [\sFmla{\False}{1.1, A \lor B}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\Box}[3]}
                ]
            ]
            [\sFmla{\True}{1, \Box B}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\lor}[2]}
            ]
        ]
    ]
]
\end{oltableau}

::: {.content-visible when-format="revealjs"}
![$(\Box A \lor \Box B) \rightarrow \Box(A \lor B)$](../images/tableaux-11/tableau-11-23.tex.svg){width=600px}
:::

False $\Box$ (line 3) introduces world 1.1 on the left branch: $A \lor B$ must be false there.

---

\begin{oltableau}
[\sFmla{\False}{1, (\Box A \lor \Box B) \rightarrow \Box(A \lor B)}, checked, just = \TAss
    [\sFmla{\True}{1, \Box A \lor \Box B}, checked, just = {\TRule{\False}{\rightarrow}[1]}
        [\sFmla{\False}{1, \Box(A \lor B)}, checked, just = {\TRule{\False}{\rightarrow}[1]}
            [\sFmla{\True}{1, \Box A}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\lor}[2]}
                [\sFmla{\False}{1.1, A \lor B}, checked, just = {\TRule{\False}{\Box}[3]}
                    [\sFmla{\True}{1.1, A}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\Box}[4]}
                        [\sFmla{\False}{1.1, A}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\lor}[5]}, close]
                    ]
                ]
            ]
            [\sFmla{\True}{1, \Box B}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\lor}[2]}
            ]
        ]
    ]
]
\end{oltableau}

::: {.content-visible when-format="revealjs"}
![$(\Box A \lor \Box B) \rightarrow \Box(A \lor B)$](../images/tableaux-11/tableau-11-24.tex.svg){width=600px}
:::

World 1.1 exists, so True $\Box$ (line 4, $\Box A$) fires: $A$ is true at 1.1. Then False $\lor$ gives $\mathbb{F}\,1.1{:}A$, clashing with line 5. Left branch closes. Now the right branch.

---

\begin{oltableau}
[\sFmla{\False}{1, (\Box A \lor \Box B) \rightarrow \Box(A \lor B)}, checked, just = \TAss
    [\sFmla{\True}{1, \Box A \lor \Box B}, checked, just = {\TRule{\False}{\rightarrow}[1]}
        [\sFmla{\False}{1, \Box(A \lor B)}, checked, just = {\TRule{\False}{\rightarrow}[1]}
            [\sFmla{\True}{1, \Box A}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\lor}[2]}
                [\sFmla{\False}{1.1, A \lor B}, checked, just = {\TRule{\False}{\Box}[3]}
                    [\sFmla{\True}{1.1, A}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\Box}[4]}
                        [\sFmla{\False}{1.1, A}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\lor}[5]}, close]
                    ]
                ]
            ]
            [\sFmla{\True}{1, \Box B}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\lor}[2]}
                [\sFmla{\False}{1.1, A \lor B}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\Box}[3]}, move by = 2
                ]
            ]
        ]
    ]
]
\end{oltableau}

::: {.content-visible when-format="revealjs"}
![$(\Box A \lor \Box B) \rightarrow \Box(A \lor B)$](../images/tableaux-11/tableau-11-25.tex.svg){width=600px}
:::

False $\Box$ (line 3) introduces world 1.1 on the right branch too: $A \lor B$ must be false there.

---

\begin{oltableau}
[\sFmla{\False}{1, (\Box A \lor \Box B) \rightarrow \Box(A \lor B)}, checked, just = \TAss
    [\sFmla{\True}{1, \Box A \lor \Box B}, checked, just = {\TRule{\False}{\rightarrow}[1]}
        [\sFmla{\False}{1, \Box(A \lor B)}, checked, just = {\TRule{\False}{\rightarrow}[1]}
            [\sFmla{\True}{1, \Box A}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\lor}[2]}
                [\sFmla{\False}{1.1, A \lor B}, checked, just = {\TRule{\False}{\Box}[3]}
                    [\sFmla{\True}{1.1, A}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\Box}[4]}
                        [\sFmla{\False}{1.1, A}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\lor}[5]}, close]
                    ]
                ]
            ]
            [\sFmla{\True}{1, \Box B}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\lor}[2]}
                [\sFmla{\False}{1.2, A \lor B}, checked, just = {\TRule{\False}{\Box}[3]}, move by = 2
                    [\sFmla{\True}{1.2, B}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\Box}[4]}
                        [\sFmla{\False}{1.2, A}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\lor}[8]}
                            [\sFmla{\False}{1.2, B}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\lor}[8]}, close]
                        ]
                    ]
                ]
            ]
        ]
    ]
]
\end{oltableau}

::: {.content-visible when-format="revealjs"}
![$(\Box A \lor \Box B) \rightarrow \Box(A \lor B)$](../images/tableaux-11/tableau-11-26.tex.svg){width=600px}
:::

This is valid in K. Intuitively, if either one of $\Box A$ or $\Box B$ is true, we can derive $\Box(A \lor B)$.
